chunks: And it is also indicated by what was narrated - Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad Al-Jawhari from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who made it upon himself to fast a month in Kufa, a month in Medina, and a month in Mecca due to a trial he was tested with. It was ruled for him that he fasted a month in Kufa, then entered Medina and fasted eighteen days there, and Al-Jamal did not stay with him. He said: 'He fasts what remains of it when he reaches his hometown.'
ai.seo_question: How to fulfill a vow of fasting in multiple cities if one cannot complete them all?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudence of *nadhr* (vows) for travelers, specifically addressing the flexibility granted when a vow specifies multiple locations. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) rules that if a person completes partial fasts in transit, the remaining obligation is consolidated and fulfilled in their home city, demonstrating the practical application of ease (*taysir*) in Shia fiqh for those burdened by travel.
